title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft from the Longue Marche period (c. 1981). It concerns the 'Hom' or injectivity part of the anabelian conjecture for Artin elementary anabelian varieties Y, namely Th. 2, cor. 1 b). Two morphisms f, g : X -> Y that induce the same (outer) map on fundamental groups should be equal.

The method uses the generalized Jacobian G = G_Y. This is an extension of an abelian variety by a torus. Y embeds in the torsor J^1_Y.
- f and g give a difference n = g - f. This is a point of G(K), where K is presumably the function field of X.
- Equality on pi_1 means n lifts to every level of the universal abelian covering. So n is in the kernel of a map (*) from G(K) to an inverse limit of H^1 / Kummer groups.
- In characteristic 0, the injectivity of (*) gives n = 0.
- The previous page notes that (*) fails in characteristic p: Kummer theory only sees the prime-to-p part, and radicial morphisms have to be inverted ('quasi-variétés').

This page:
(1) Grothendieck hopes the injectivity of (*) might nevertheless hold without any characteristic hypothesis, to be examined.
(2) In characteristic p > 0, with prime-to-p fundamental groups, the argument only shows that n is a p-power torsion point of G(K).
(3) If G is a torus, n = 0 and so f = g. This happens when all the successive 'fibres' of the elementary fibration Y are of genus 0, i.e. punctured P^1's. The reason is that a torus over a field of characteristic p has no nontrivial p-power torsion rational points (mu_{p^r}(K) = 1).
(4) In general the arithmetic argument proves, pointwise and a fortiori, the following. Let x be in X, P = f(x), Q = g(x).
- Q - P is p-power torsion in G_Y.
- For every finite étale Galois cover Y' -> Y of degree prime to p, and every P' over P, there is Q' over Q with Q' - P' p-power torsion in G_{Y'}.
He does not see how to deduce P = Q from this 'tower of p-torsion' condition. The struck-out lines show an abandoned attempt using the prime-to-p isogenies n_G and division points Q_n with n.Q_n = Q.
(5) The oblique margin says the 'thesis' (the anabelian injectivity statement) seems certainly true over a base of characteristic p, once fundamental groups in the definitions are replaced by their prime-to-p quotients; there is an obscure allusion to Witt.

The next page abandons the arithmetic route. It gives a geometric proof: if a translation u of the generalized Jacobian maps a nonempty open U of Y into Y, then u = 0. The proof goes by dévissage to curves; for complete curves of genus >= 2 it uses the Lefschetz fixed-point formula (a fixed-point-free automorphism would need Lefschetz number 2 - 2g = 0), and for the toric part an explicit argument with the lambda_i. This sidesteps the p-torsion problem left open here.
errors: Logically the cover Y' in 'rev. étale galoisien fini Y' de X' must be a cover of Y, not X, since P' lies over P in Y and G_{Y'} is its generalized Jacobian. This is probably a slip of the pen or a misreading.

Without the radicial/quasi-variety modification (previous page), the statement in characteristic p is false as it stands: Frobenius-twisted maps induce the same maps on pi_1. Grothendieck is aware of this, but this page does not repeat the caveat.

The pointwise 'tower' criterion is left unproved (Grothendieck says he cannot deduce P = Q). The step from a statement about n in G(K) to pointwise statements for every x is plausible but not justified on the page.
The struck text 'premier à G' should read 'premier à p'.

ideas.what: Injectivity of the Kummer-type map G(K) -> lim H^1 for generalized Jacobians, used to prove the Hom-injectivity part of the anabelian conjecture, and its failure or prime-to-p restriction in characteristic p
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of the Kummer map / divisible elements in Mordell-Weil of semi-abelian varieties; 'Hom-conjecture' injectivity (f, g inducing the same pi_1-map implies f = g)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Anabelian injectivity is folklore and standard: Grothendieck's 1983 Faltings letter; Tamagawa and Mochizuki for the proofs in the relevant settings. Mordell-Weil/Kummer injectivity is classical (Lang-Néron, Faltings).
ideas.where_published: The anabelian Hom-conjecture is in the letter to Faltings (1983) and in the Esquisse; this specific Kummer/generalized-Jacobian argument is unsure

ideas.what: In char p with prime-to-p pi_1, the obstruction is exactly p-power torsion; for a torus (genus 0 fibres) it vanishes because mu_{p^r}(K) = 1
ideas.modern_name: No p-torsion in tori in characteristic p; prime-to-p (tame) anabelian geometry in positive characteristic
ideas.usually_credited_to: Elementary fact; prime-to-p/tame anabelian results in char p are due to Tamagawa, Stix, Saïdi-Tamagawa

ideas.what: Criterion: if Q - P is p-power torsion in G_Y and the same holds for suitable lifts in all prime-to-p Galois étale covers Y', then P = Q (posed, not proved)
ideas.modern_name: 'Torsion packets in towers' / separation of points by prime-to-p covers modulo p-torsion; related to Manin-Mumford in char p (Pink-Roessler) and Raynaud-type results
ideas.usually_credited_to: Not known as a named statement; neighbouring results by Raynaud (theta divisor, covers), Pink-Roessler (Manin-Mumford in char p), Tamagawa (prime-to-p anabelian results)

ideas.what: The geometric replacement (next page): a translation of the generalized Jacobian preserving an open of an anabelian curve is trivial, via Lefschetz 2 - 2g != 0
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of the Abel-Jacobi embedding under translations

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, and leaves open, a pointwise 'p-torsion in all prime-to-p covers' criterion meant to force P = Q for an anabelian variety in characteristic p. As a standalone Diophantine/anabelian statement it does not seem to appear in the literature: points whose differences remain p-power torsion in the generalized Jacobians of all prime-to-p Galois covers must coincide.
missed.quote: pour tout rev. étale galoisien fini Y' de X, de degré premier à p, et tout point P' au-dessus de P, il existe Q' au-dessus de Q tel que Q'-P' soit un élément de p-torsion de G_{Y'} ... Je ne [vois?] ... en déduire P=Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a clean question bridging prime-to-p anabelian geometry in characteristic p with p-torsion behaviour of Jacobians in towers of covers (Hasse-Witt/p-rank growth, Pink-Roessler). It could still be investigated, though the Hom-injectivity it was meant to serve is obtained more simply by the geometric Lefschetz argument on the next page.

missed.claim: Grothendieck speculates that the injectivity of the Kummer-type map (*) might hold without a characteristic hypothesis.
missed.quote: est cependant possible que l'injectivité de (*) reste valable sans hyp. de caractéristique — à examiner de plus près
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. In char p, p-divisibility phenomena (e.g. non-reduced p-torsion, Frobenius) make it doubtful in naive form, and the previous page already records a counterexample-type remark for elliptic curves.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of a standard step (Hom-injectivity via generalized Jacobians) in the anabelian program. The characteristic-p reduction to p-torsion and the torus case are routine. The open pointwise 'p-torsion in all prime-to-p covers' criterion is a mildly interesting unpublished question, but Grothendieck himself bypasses it the next page with a classical geometric argument.
transcription_corrections: 'rev. étale galoisien fini Y' de X' — mathematically should be 'de Y'; the image reading 'de X' is uncertain.
'(il y a/suffit[?] pour cela' — likely '(il suffit pour cela que les "fibres" de la variété élémentaire Y soient de genre 0)'.
Struck line '(premier à G)' — should read '(n premier à p)'.
'Je ne pourrait[?] que[?] puisse[?] en déduire P=Q' — plausibly 'Je ne vois pas [comment] en déduire P=Q' or 'Je ne pense pas qu'on puisse en déduire P=Q'; the image is ambiguous.

Oblique margin is roughly: 'Dans ce cas il semble certainement que la thèse soit vraie sur un corps de base de car. p>0, en remplaçant les groupes fondamentaux dans la définition [des variétés anabéliennes] par leurs quotients premiers à p ...'; the remainder is largely illegible.
